trust_decision.summary: Whether an authenticated caller may adopt a guest cart is decided by possession of the cart's own token (x-spree-token), not by the JWT plus a cart prefixed ID: the guard lives in Spree::Api::V3::Store::CartsController#associate and tests the header against @cart.token before Spree::Cart::Associate is called.

landing_point.why: The advisory names PATCH /api/v3/store/carts/:id/associate, and that action's only lookup at the pinned commit, find_cart_for_association (carts_controller.rb:173-175), filters by store and by user but never by the cart token, so the prefixed ID alone selects the victim guest cart.

fix_sites.module_kind: private guard method in the same controller

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Spree::Order#associate_user! is an internal model API that also backs the staff path (Spree::Admin::Orders::UserController, admin/app/controllers/spree/admin/orders/user_controller.rb:16,44,57), so a solver can argue the cart-token check belongs at the HTTP boundary where the header exists and that the model/service layer was never in the advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A signed-in customer keeps full JWT-only access to their own cart: GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v3/store/carts/:id and the nested items/payments routes must not start requiring x-spree-token, because CartResolvable#find_cart!/find_cart authorize by ownership OR token. A fix that hoists the token requirement into find_cart! or a controller-wide before_action breaks every own-cart request.

O6_input_shapes: x-spree-token header absent on a guest cart
x-spree-token equal to the cart token
x-spree-token not equal to the cart token
caller already owns the cart and sends no token
caller already owns the cart and sends the cart token (re-associate)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PATCH /admin/orders/:order_id/user reassigns an order to a customer by calling @order.associate_user! with no cart-token check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin-only route already gated by authorize! :update_customer (user_controller.rb:94-96); staff hold no x-spree-token and are trusted to reassign carts, so the claim credential is meaningless there.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package away (spree/admin vs spree/api), single file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cart merge on login: Spree::Order#merge! delegates to Spree::OrderMerger, whose set_user claims the surviving guest order via associate_user! with no token check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The only caller in the pinned tree is the legacy controller concern Spree::Core::ControllerHelpers::Order#set_current_order (spree/core/lib/spree/core/controller_helpers/order.rb:53-76), which no v3 controller includes; a solver can call it dead/legacy code and out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: two packages away (spree/api -> spree/core), separate file from the O2 site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A token: argument on the Spree::Cart::Associate service that rejects a claim when the token does not match the guest order
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The service is the single sink named by the fix's own comment ('the token... is the claim credential'); a maintainer hardening the service instead of the controller would leave the admin caller needing an explicit bypass.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A POST /api/v3/store/customer/orders/:id/claim action that reuses cart_associate_service for a cart the shopper built before logging in
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The customer-namespaced surface already exists (routes: spree/api/config/routes.rb:70-84) and the SDK exposes customer-namespaced calls, so a second claim endpoint there is a natural place a maintainer would add.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The same token requirement applied to POST /api/v3/store/carts/:id/complete, the other member action that acts on a cart by prefixed ID
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: complete already re-authorizes by token only on its rescue branch (carts_controller.rb:118-122), so a maintainer tightening cart possession would plausibly extend the guard to the whole member surface.

O9_family: CWE-639 improper authorization / insecure direct object reference (broken object-level access control) on guest cart claim

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby 4.0, Rails ~> 8.1.0 (MySQL job pins 7.2.0), bundler with a Gemfile per gem (spree/core, spree/api, spree/admin, spree/emails), `rake test_app` to generate the dummy Rails app, RSpec + rswag; TypeScript packages under packages/ are separate (pnpm) and not needed here
O10_build.project_tests: spree/api/spec/controllers/spree/api/v3/store/carts_controller_spec.rb (describe 'PATCH #associate', lines 724-821) and the rswag request spec spree/api/spec/integration/spree/api/v3/store/carts_spec.rb

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a controller-wide `before_action :require_cart_token!` (or move the check into CartResolvable#find_cart!), which makes JWT-only access to the caller's own cart fail on show/update/destroy.

out_of_scope_notes: docs/api-reference/storefront.yaml:679-690 still documents the legacy v2 route PATCH /api/v2/storefront/cart/associate (which takes an order token); that controller is not in this repository, so it was not pursued.
